sentences.text:
Case :- Matters Under Article 227 No. - 257 of 2025
Petitioner :- Smt. Nisha Rani @ Prachi

Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Petitioner :- Ajay Singh Yadav
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Present petition has been preferred with the prayer to set aside the impugned order dated
27.9.2024 passed by the Sessions Judge, Ghaziabad in Criminal Revision No.531 of 2024,
computerized Registration No.532 of 2024 computerized Registration No.532 of 2024 (Dayanand
vs. State of U.P. and another), under Section 397 of Cr.P.C, Police Station Vijainagar, District
Ghaziabad, arising out of order dated 4.7.2024 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Court No.2, Ghaziabad in Case No.3599 of 2023 (State vs. Dayanand) in relation to Case Crime
No.160 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 34 of Ipc and Section 3/4 of Dowry

Prohibition Act, Police Station Kotwali Vijainagar, District Ghaziabad.

3.  The case of the petitioner is that she lodged a first information report dated 3.3.2023, after registration of the F.I.R, the concerned Investigating Officer has investigated the matter and recorded the statement of petitioner under Section 161 Cr.P.C, after investigation, I.O, concerned has submitted the charge sheet against accused/opposite party no.2 in aforesaid case crime no. and took cognizance on 27.7.2023, however, rest of the accused were exonerated, where after opposite party no.2 moved a discharge application before the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Court No.2, Ghaziabad for discharging him in the said case.

entities.text:
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Court No.2, Ghaziabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned additional C.J.M has rejected the discharge application filed by opposite party no.2 by order dated 4.7.2024.
Being aggrieved from the order dated 4.7.2024, opposite party no.2 has preferred a criminal revision before the court of learned Sessions Judge, Ghaziabad which was allowed by order dated 27.9.2024.
Being aggrieved with the order dated 27.9.2024, petitioner preferred the instant petition before this court.
4. While challenging the order dated 27.09.2024, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that it has been passed without going through the record.
5. Per contra, learned AGA vehemently opposed the prayer sought through the instant petition.

6. After hearing the rival submissions extended by learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, this Court finds that order impugned has been passed after considering the material available on record and no prejudice is caused to the petitioner with the order impugned through which the matter has been only remanded back by learned revisional court to the concerned learned trial court for deciding afresh the discharge application preferred by the accused opposite party no.2.
7.
In view of the aforementioned facts and circumstances, the instant petition lacks merit and stands dismissed accordingly.
